analysis.investment_thesis: All Time Plastics is a simple, understandable household plastics business with decent ROE (19%) and low leverage (D/E 0.22), but it operates in a commodity-like category with thin 10% operating margins and no durable moat. At 36.5x earnings following a fresh IPO capital raise (equity jumped from INR 202 Cr to 594 Cr in 2025), the price offers no margin of safety.
key_strengths: Clean balance sheet: D/E 0.22, promoter holding 70%, 60+ year operating history since 1964
ROE of 19% and 3Y net profit CAGR of 24% shows improving economics
Simple, understandable business with export diversification (EU/UK/US)
key_risks: Commodity plastic goods with no pricing power vs. Cello, Milton, Wim Plast — ROCE only 13.9%
Fresh IPO priced at 36.5x P/E — classic "IPO hype" territory Buffett avoids
Capex-heavy: FCF swung to -INR 62 Cr in 2025 on INR 114 Cr capex, raw material (plastic/crude) cost volatility
red_flags: Recent IPO with equity nearly tripling in 2025 — Buffett's rule: be skeptical of IPOs
Operating margin 10% is thin for a "branded" consumer company, indicating weak moat
ROCE (13.9%) meaningfully below ROE (19%) suggests returns flatter at the asset level
analysis.detailed_analysis:
This is the kind of business I can understand — plastic buckets, containers, hangers — but understanding a business is not the same as wanting to own it. The numbers tell me this is a decent, not wonderful, enterprise: revenue compounding at ~12%, operating margins stuck around 10%, and ROCE of just 13.9%. In branded household goods, the real winners (think See's Candies-style economics) earn 20%+ operating margins with negative working capital. All Time is competing against Cello, Milton, and cheap unbranded imports in a category where the consumer rarely pays up for the label on a chopping board. That's not a moat; that's a treadmill.

The valuation seals it. 36.5x earnings for an 11.9% topline grower in a capital-intensive, commodity-input business is the sort of price Mr. Market offers when recency bias meets IPO euphoria — note the equity base tripled in 2025, clearly an IPO raise, and free cash flow promptly went negative on a INR 114 Cr capex bill. I don't need to form a view on whether management deploys that capital well; I just need to know I'm being asked to pay ahead of the evidence. Pass, and revisit only if the price halves or the business proves it has pricing power through a full cycle.
